title: Pauri 32, sound: ik doo jeebhau
tomorrow: Pauri 32, meaning: the steps of the ladder

lines: A TONGUE INSTEAD OF A NUMBER.
cards: Listen to a small child tell a parent how much they love them. I love you a hundred. No, a thousand.
A million, a billion, infinity. Infinity plus one. The numbers climb because the feeling is bigger than any number they know.
Grown-ups smile, but the child has found something true: when love runs past what you can say, you reach for the biggest counting word there is, and then go past it.
Guru Nanak does something like this in Pauri 32, with a tongue instead of a number. It opens a new stretch of Japji, the ladder and the realms. Today, how it sounds.

teach.h: IK DOO JEEBHAU — FROM ONE TONGUE.
teach.b: Here is the opening: ik doo jeebhau lakh hohi, lakh hoveh lakh vees. Ik: one. Doo: from, out of.
Jeebhau: tongue. So, from one tongue. Lakh: a hundred thousand; in South Asia people still count in lakhs, the way Americans count in thousands.
Hohi: become. From one tongue, let there be a hundred thousand.

Then Nanak goes past it: lakh hoveh lakh vees, let those hundred thousand become twenty times a hundred thousand. That's two million tongues, the child's infinity plus one in a poet's language. Now listen.
Ik doo jeebhau: three light steps, then a vowel that opens, jee-bhau. Lakh hohi: short and hard.
Then lakh hoveh lakh vees, lakh sounding twice like a drumbeat getting faster. You can hear the numbers pile up. What will all those tongues do?
That's tomorrow, along with a word that tells you where this stanza is going. For today, notice the wish.

teach.h: A WISH FOR MORE WAYS TO SAY IT.
teach.b: It isn't for more money, or more time, or more of anything for oneself.
It's a wish for more ways to say one thing.

how: Many Sikhs recite Japji Sahib each morning; Pauri 32 opens the stretch many teachers call the ladder and the realms, and it opens with the image of a single tongue multiplied into two million.

o: a lucky mark or sign drawn for blessing
a crowd too big for anyone to count

games.q: you've been given one tongue. in the opening of Pauri 32, what does Nanak wish for?
o: a hundred thousand tongues, then two million.
a tongue that speaks every language.
games.why: ik doo jeebhau lakh hohi, lakh hoveh lakh vees. tomorrow: what all those tongues would do.

practice: Say the first line aloud three times, slowly, letting each lakh land like a drumbeat: ik doo jeebhau lakh hohi, lakh hoveh lakh vees. Then close your mouth and let your one tongue rest, soft, behind your teeth, doing nothing.
Breathe through your nose, and let any thought pass without saying it.

wordCard.voice: Lakh, a hundred thousand. It opens with a wish: from one tongue, a hundred thousand, and then two million. The first stanza of the ladder.

orig.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 32: from one tongue, let there be a hundred thousand.

carryVoice: Your line: ik doo jeebhau, from one tongue. The next stanzas climb from this wish. See you tomorrow.
